size.note: Adult doe. Head and body about 1.3-1.6 m; 0.9-1.0 m at the shoulder. The build script scales the mesh to 0.95 m at the withers, the top of the back over the fore legs as client/src/lineupAnimals.js measures it (until 2026-10-25 it scaled the Neck1 joint to 0.95 m, which sits ~0.2 m lower, so the drawn doe stood 1.17 m). Measured on the lineup (2026-10-25): withers 0.95 m, top of the ears 1.35 m, nose to tail tip 1.34 m, head and body 1.19 m (rest pose, head up, measured along the ground: shorter than the brief's 1.5 m because the source model is leggy and short in the body).

rig: skinned (2026-10-27): the source's 46-joint skin kept as JOINTS_0 / WEIGHTS_0 and its clips baked by tools/bake_clips.py (recipe library/animals/clips/odocoileus_hemionus.json) into client/assets/deer_clips.bin + .json (Idle, Idle_2, Idle_Headlow, Eating, Walk, Gallop, and a synthetic bedded frame); drawn by animalModels.js's skin path, one draw call a tier. The procedural part rig (_PART, _PARTW, _PIVOT: legs A/B in a diagonal walk, tail, head) stays on the file as the fallback when the clip set fails to load (?deer=proc draws the procedural deer)

size.note: 5% larger than the doe at the withers (0.9975 m, the doe's 0.95; measured on the lineup 2026-10-25: withers 1.00 m, top of the antlers 1.55 m, nose to tail tip 1.40 m, head and body 1.24 m). Until 2026-10-25 the Neck1 joint was scaled to 0.9975 m and the drawn buck stood 1.24 m at the withers.

buck.changes: neck 1.15x thicker about the neck line; darker forehead (#3b2c22); hooves and pasterns go with their leg part (the doe leaves them on the body, a doe fault left alone so the doe's output does not change); procedural mule-deer antlers built per tier and never decimated with the body: burr on the frontal bone in front of and inside the ear base, the beam up, out and back, an even fork at about 45% of its length, the rear branch forking again (mature 3x3), a small brow tine; tubes 2.5 to 0.5 cm, 6-sided on lod0, 3-sided with 1 cm minimum radius on lod1, one flat V per side on lod2; hard-antler colour burr #6b5843 to tip #d9ceb5
buck.antler_flags: _ANTLER: 0 off the antler, else 0.05 + 0.95 x the fraction of the way from burr to tip (growth, shedding, velvet thickening, colour); _TINE: 0 beam and main fork, 1 the rear branch's second fork (hide it for a forked-horn 2x2), 2 brow tine, 3 burr ring. extras.antler_burr holds the left burr centre (glTF axes; the right mirrors in x). Antler vertices are HEAD (6), weight 1, pivot Neck1.
buck.season: spring antlerless (collapse every antler vertex to its burr, keep tine 3 as the pedicel knob), April-August velvet (grey-brown, about 1.3x thicker about the burr, rounded tips), September-January hard, cast January-March (brief)
buck.accuracy_notes: Reads as an antlered black-tailed buck from the side, front and above: a forked rack sweeping out and back inside the ear spread, darker forehead, thicker neck. The rack is a construction from straight segments, so it reads geometric close up; the rut neck swell and stained hocks are not modelled; the body is the doe's scaled 5%. At a full graze dip (head flick 1.5 rad) the lowest antler point stays 0.63 m above the ground (0.92 m at 1.0 rad).
buck.clips: the doe's clip set (same skeleton), the translation column scaled by 1.045; antler vertices skinned to the Head joint

accuracy_notes: Source is a generic stylised deer. The build script fixes what reads wrong for a Sierra foothill black-tailed doe: ears enlarged 1.3x (mule and black-tailed deer have big ears), grey-brown coat with a darker forehead and nose bridge, small dark almond eye, tail black on top and at the tip and white beneath, a clean white rump patch. The buck is a variant (variants.buck, client/assets/deer_buck.glb). Since 2026-10-27 the deer is drawn skinned from the source's own clips (hooves on their IK bones swing with the legs and plant on the ground at a walk; the bedded frame lies on folded legs); on the part-rig fallback the doe's hooves still stay with the body and the bedded pose sinks. The low-poly faceting is stylised rather than realistic. A local naturalist should check tail, rump and ear proportions against does seen in the foothills.

clips.notes: no trot and no bedded clip in the source: the Walk is hurried for a trot (capped at 2.6 Hz) and the bed is one synthetic frame (fore knees forward on the ground, cannons back under the chest, hind legs tucked forward, dropped 0.45 m); the Walk's stride is 0.65 m a cycle (authored at 0.56 m/s, so the game's 1.1 m/s walk runs it at 1.7 Hz)
